svg.title: Three text-triggered guards collapsing into one destination-triggered question
svg.desc: Three boxes across the top -- the safety gate, staged dictation and the no-text-target guard -- each triggered by a property of the transcribed text. Arrows from all three converge on a single box asking what the text is about to enter, fed from the left by inject/target.py, which already resolves the focused element. That question branches to two outcomes: confirm first for a high-cost destination such as a terminal or a payment field, and inject directly for an ordinary one. The proposal replaces three triggers with one question rather than adding a fourth guard.
svg.title: cmdsafety holds rm -rf, mkfs, a force-push, pending a spoken confirm.
staged buffers so a confirm is not swallowed as ordinary text.
When the focused element is not editable, the text goes to the clipboard.
svg.text: three triggers, all asking about the text
svg.title: The destination decides the confirmation. This is the only new part.
svg.text: one question: what is this about to enter?
a terminal, a payment field, a chat box
svg.title: Already shipped: TargetDetector resolves the focused element via AT-SPI, falling back to xdotool on X11.
svg.text: the metric falls out: an error scored by where it landed
